findings.message: The acceptance-gate confirms SPEC-1/2/5/6/8/11 are still tautological after this change: the baseline artifact already satisfies `(.result_contract == 2) and has("test_output")`, so a regression that drops result_contract back to v1 or removes top-level fields will still pass these guards, leaving the production schema contract undetected.

SPEC-11 integration guard has the same tautology: if the baseline artifact already carries result_contract=2, the compound jq expression is satisfied regardless of whether the implementation change is present, removing the regression signal for v2 schema shape on the summary-format path.

SPEC-11 unit guard now asserts `(.result_contract == 2) and (.run_mode == "full")` but the acceptance-gate reports it is still tautological, meaning a writer regression that omits result_contract or emits v1 shape will not be caught by this suite.

SPEC-8 still concatenates two unrelated checks into a single string (`"interrupted|true"`); when the assertion fires on-call, the failure message provides no indication of which sub-check (signal mapping or contract version) failed, slowing incident diagnosis.

No assertion verifies that top-level exit_code and data.exit_code carry the same value; if a code path updates one but not the other, downstream consumers reading different paths will silently diverge with no test signal (gap persists from prior change).
